n: The angel turns Nephi’s attention far into the future, beyond his own people, to many nations and kingdoms.
Again the angel teaches by asking Nephi to describe what he sees.
These are the nations of the Gentiles — peoples not of Israelite descent. Much of what follows concerns Europe and, later, the Americas.

f.g: In the Book of Mormon, usually non-Israelite nations, especially those from Europe who later settled the Americas.

n: Nephi sees a great “church” forming among the Gentiles. In this vision the word stands for any organization or system opposed to God, not one specific denomination.
The angel calls it the most abominable church because it persecutes, tortures, and enslaves God’s faithful people. A “yoke of iron” pictures harsh, unbreakable bondage.
Its true founder is the devil. Whatever form it takes, its source is opposition to God.

f.w: the devil that he was the founder of it

n: Nephi sees wealth, luxurious clothing, and harlots. These images, also found in Revelation, symbolize greed, worldliness, and immorality.
The angel explains that riches, fine clothing, and sexual sin are what this church truly desires — its goals are worldly, not godly.

f.w: the desires of this great and abominable church

n: It persecutes the saints in order to win the world’s praise. Seeking human approval at any cost is a mark of this church.

f.w: for the praise of the world

n: Nephi sees “many waters” — an ocean — separating the Gentile nations from his brothers’ descendants in the promised land.

f.g: The Atlantic Ocean separating Europe from the Americas.

n: The angel says God’s wrath is upon the Lamanite descendants because of their unbelief.

Nephi sees a man among the Gentiles, moved by the Spirit of God, who crosses the ocean to the promised land. Many Latter-day Saints, including Church leaders, have identified him as Christopher Columbus, who described feeling divinely led.

The Spirit moves other Gentiles too, and they leave “captivity” — often understood as the religious and political oppression of Europe — to cross the ocean. This fits colonists such as the Pilgrims seeking freedom.

f.w: they went forth out of captivity

n: Large numbers of Gentiles settle the promised land, and the descendants of Lehi’s people are scattered and struck down before them. Nephi sees, with sorrow, the suffering of native peoples.

f.w: scattered before the Gentiles and were smitten

n: The Gentile settlers prosper and take the land as their inheritance. Nephi compares their appearance to his own people before their destruction.

f.w: obtain the land for their inheritance

n: These settlers humble themselves before the Lord, and His power is with them.

f.w: did humble themselves before the Lord

n: Their “mother Gentiles” — the nations they came from — gather by land and sea to fight them. Many readers see the American Revolutionary War, when Britain fought its colonies.

f.g: The parent nations, especially Great Britain.

n: God’s power is with the colonists, and His wrath is upon those who fight against them.

f.w: the power of God was with them

n: Nephi sees the colonists delivered by God from all other nations — the birth of a free nation in the promised land.

f.w: delivered by the power of God

n: As they prosper, a book goes forth among them. This is the Bible, which was widely read in colonial America.
The angel asks whether Nephi knows what the book means.
Nephi admits he does not. His honesty invites further teaching.

The angel explains: it is a record of the Jews containing the Lord’s covenants with Israel and many prophecies. It resembles the brass plates Lehi’s family carried, though shorter, and it is of great worth to the Gentiles.

f.g: The Bible, especially the Old Testament.

n: When it first came from the Jews — including the writings of the apostles — the record contained the fulness of the gospel and testified truly of Christ.
At first these sacred writings passed in purity from the Jews to the Gentiles.

After the apostles carried the gospel to the Gentiles, the great and abominable church arose and removed many “plain and precious” parts of the gospel, including covenants. This is a key Book of Mormon teaching about why a restoration of truth was needed.
These changes were made on purpose — to twist the Lord’s ways and to blind and harden people.

f.w: pervert the right ways of the Lord

n: The angel summarizes: after the book passed through that church, many plain and precious things had been removed. Latter-day Saints believe the Bible is the word of God “as far as it is translated correctly,” and Joseph Smith’s inspired revision (JST) restored some lost material.

f.w: many plain and precious things taken away

n: This long verse explains the result: the Bible spreads to every Gentile nation, even to America, but because clear truths have been lost, a great many people stumble in confusion, and Satan gains great power over them.

f.w: plainness which is in the Lamb of God

n: Even so, the Lord will not allow the Gentiles in the promised land to wipe out Lehi’s descendants. The land was covenanted to Lehi’s family, and a mixed remnant of Nephite blood will survive among the Lamanites.

f.g: Nephite descendants who survived mixed among the Lamanites.

n: Nor will the Lord let the Gentiles destroy the Lamanites entirely.

f.w: destroy the seed of thy brethren

n: God will not leave the Gentiles forever in spiritual blindness caused by the lost truths. Help is coming.
Christ Himself speaks through the angel: He will show mercy to the Gentiles even while He judges the remnant of Israel.

f.w: I will be merciful unto the Gentiles

n: After Lehi’s descendants are judged and the Gentiles stumble, Christ promises to bring forth, by His own power, much more of His gospel in plain and precious form. Latter-day Saints see this as the Restoration, including the Book of Mormon.

Christ will show Himself to Nephi’s descendants, and they will write what He teaches. After their downfall, these records will be hidden, then brought forth to the Gentiles by the gift and power of God — exactly how the Book of Mormon describes its own origin.

f.w: I will manifest myself unto thy seed
by the gift and power of the Lamb

n: These records will contain Christ’s gospel, His “rock,” and His salvation — the sure foundation for faith.
Those who work to build Zion in that day will receive the Holy Ghost, and if they endure they will be saved. The last line quotes Isaiah: the feet of messengers bringing good news are beautiful.

f.g: The pure in heart; a people united in righteousness.

n: Nephi sees the Bible coming from the Gentiles to the remnant of his brothers’ descendants.

f.w: the book of the Lamb of God

n: Then “other books” come forth by Christ’s power — the Book of Mormon and other latter-day scripture — to convince Gentiles, Lehi’s descendants, and scattered Jews that the Bible’s prophets and apostles are true.
These last records will confirm the Bible, restore lost truths, and teach all people that Jesus is the Son of the Eternal Father and Savior of the world, and that all must come to Him to be saved.

f.w: shall establish the truth of the first

f.g: The Book of Mormon’s title page states the same purpose: to convince Jew and Gentile that Jesus is the Christ.

n: The Bible and the Book of Mormon will be “established in one.” Together they testify of the one God and one Shepherd over all the earth.

Christ will reveal Himself to all nations. The order reverses: in His mortal ministry the gospel went first to the Jews, then the Gentiles; in the last days it goes first to the Gentiles, then the Jews.

f.w: the last shall be first, and the first shall be last
